newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index falls 1.85 pct, ends near day's lows.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index falls 1.85 pct, ends near day's lows.

text.p: ** (1005 GMT) - Shares at Bombay exchange close near day's
low, speculator-led selling pulls down market
** Bombay's benchmark 30-share index falls 69.24 points, or
** Dull institutional trade on last day of weekly account
at Bombay bourse, holiday at National Stock Exchange
** Foreign funds in holiday mood, long Easter week-end
Shares suffered fresh losses on Friday as speculators sold at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on a day clouded by a holiday mood, dealers said.
"Institutions are not active in the market. This fall has taken everyone by surprise," said Sanjay Vaid, chief dealer at local firm, Lloyds Securities.
The absence of any fund activity ahead of the long Easter week-end and a holiday at the National Stock Exchange prompted bear operators to offload stocks in a big way, dealers said.
The sharp sell-off pulled down Bombay's top-30 index to shed nearly 70 points or 1.85 percent to close near the day's lows.
The end of the weekly trade account at the Bombay exchange on Friday led to some squaring off by operators, dealers said.
"There might have been a lot of squaring-off of outstanding positions by market players near end of trade," said Ajit Ambani, a BSE member-broker.
The Bombay index has lost nearly 64 points, or 1.71 percent, in the week ending Friday amid a price consolidation in the market.
"We feel bear operators have taken advantage of a dull day and hammered prices to create some sort of a shaky market mood," said an equities dealer at a foreign brokerage.
Trading volumes were low because of Good Friday holiday for banks, government offices and the National Stock Exchange which operates from more than 100 centres across India, traders said.
"It has been really boring trading day. The market weakness near the close of the session lacked any fund based selling," the dealer at the foreign brokerage said.
Shares of shoe-maker Bata India ended 4.25 rupees, or 6.4 percent, higher at 71.0 rupees after the firm on Thursday announced profits.
Bata India unveiled a net profit of 41.5 million rupees for calendar 1996 against net loss of 421.6 million rupees in 1995.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
